name: The Interview
tagline: Each round is an issue: one question at full volume, the agent's verdict as a pull-quote, your reply as a first-class voice, and everything decided typeset as the record.
model: Editorial interview: filmstrip of the round on top, one question per page, verdict-first choices, a flip-over record, and the visual as a captioned plate.
philosophy: A grill is a conversation about decisions, so the page is typeset like an interview rather than laid out like an inbox. Hierarchy comes from scale first: the question at 58px, the agent's recommendation as an italic pull-quote with its why and cost right under it, the alternatives beside it, and everything else in a margin. Red is the only colour and it means one thing: not yet printed (staged, reopened, stale, new recommendation). Black is settled, grey is parked. The record and the plate are not panes; they are pages you flip to with one key and back with Esc.

principles.decision: Each page reads top-down as question, then the recommendation as a pull-quote with WHY and COST split out, then the alternatives, then the actions. The cost sentence is detected from the rec's why and labelled in red so the trade-off is never buried.

principles.principle: Hierarchy by scale and weight before colour
principles.decision: Newsreader display at 58px for the question, 28px italic for the verdict, 17px for other options, 12px mono for kickers. One accent (vermilion) carries only the not-yet-settled states; decided is plain ink.

principles.principle: Hick's law and one primary action per view
principles.decision: The recommendation is the first choice (keys 1 and a), the remaining options are listed under 'Or instead', and there is exactly one path for writing: 'Object, or answer in your own words' (r). Send is the single dark block in the corner.

The kicker names what the question hangs off (Q9 What Finish writes) and the margin prints that dependency's actual decision; the strip shows every frame of the round with its state word, so you never remember where you are.

principles.principle: Preattentive state encoding and Gestalt common region
principles.decision: Open, staged, decided, deferred, reopened and new-rec are words plus one hue plus one form: staged edits are red proofreader marks (open ^ B) in the send bar, reopened gets a red band above the title that says 'Not settled', decided gets an ink band.

Every action shows its key as a keycap; staging changes the option row, the strip frame, the counts and the send bar in the same beat; Send toasts 'Sent N actions as one turn' and the masthead lamp pulses while the agent works; Explore sends at once with an Undo toast.
Send is a full-height black block pinned to the bottom-right corner of the viewport, with ⌘↵ printed on it.

The record is a typeset document of statements ('Transport: "Simpler: the web app writes to a local JSON..."', 'Chose B over the recommended A', 'Locked'), grouped by round with the agent's refinement under each, filtered as you type.

fixes.finding: Capability 2: states must be unmistakable, reopened must not read as settled
fixes.how: State is always a word, never a dot: the strip frame shows OPEN / STAGED / DECIDED / DEFERRED / REOPENED, NEW REC; the page opens with a red band 'Reopened by the agent at 22:44. Not settled.' quoting the old answer and the agent's reason; the record strikes the old statement through and prints the reopen note in red italic; a new recommendation is tagged 'updated' in red beside 'The agent recommends'.

fixes.finding: Capability 3: pick 1-4, accept, one unambiguous way to write, defer, reopen, explore, thread with staged messages
fixes.how: The pull-quote is option 1/a; other options keyed by their letter position; one 'Object, or answer in your own words' path (r, f is an alias) opens a red-ruled voice block directly under the question, Enter stages it; d defers; o on a decided question opens the same voice block as a reopen note; e sends 'explore deeper' at once with a 5 s Undo; the margin thread shows AGENT/YOU entries with times and staged messages in red italic marked 'staged'.

fixes.finding: Capability 4: live counts, auto-advance, unstage, clear Send summary
fixes.how: The strip header counts open / staged / reopened in tabular numerals and ticks as you stage; after any stage the page slides to the next unstaged open or reopened question; u unstages; the send bar lists every staged edit as a proofreader mark (Q18 open ^ accept A) and the button reads 'Send 3 as one turn'.

fixes.finding: Capability 5: visual with two-way linkage and redraw when stale
fixes.how: One sandboxed iframe is drawn as a small plate in the margin and expands to a full spread on v; hovering a frame, dependency or figure caption posts {highlight}; the child posts {clicked} and the page jumps to that question and takes keyboard focus back; figure pins (Q1, Q12, Q15...) are placed from the child's region boxes; the stale banner names which reopened question invalidated it and 'Visualize again' (shift+v) redraws to v4 after the working state.

fixes.finding: Capability 8: find a past decision in one look or one action
fixes.how: l flips to the record: a document with summary numerals (14 decided, 6 locked, 2 reopened...), a round index, and one statement per question; typing 'transport' filters live to 'Q2 Transport: "Simpler: the web app writes to a local JSON..." In your own words, instead of the recommended A. AGENT 21:11 Refinement: two files...'; Enter opens it on the stage. Dependencies in the kicker and margin also open the record at that decision.

tradeoffs: One question per page means you cannot scan a whole round's option texts at once; the strip gives states and titles only, and you clear the round by moving through it.
The margin plate is a picture, not a hit target (the iframe is pointer-events:none while small); region clicks need the full plate (v), which is one extra key.
Editorial scale eats vertical room: with the reply open at 1440x900 the options drop just below the fold until you stage or close it.
The record is a filtered document rather than a graph; the dependency graph appears only locally (hangs off / feeds), not as a drawn tree.
bestFor: A developer clearing a round of 7-8 questions from the keyboard who wants to read the agent's verdict and cost at a glance, object in their own words without hunting for a textarea, and re-read what was decided as prose rather than as a list of cards.

palette.name: Vermilion
palette.role: the only accent: staged, reopened, stale, new rec, cost (5.2:1 on page)

type: Newsreader (Google Fonts, static latin instances): opsz 72 at 400 and 300 for display (question 58px at 1440, 50px at 1280, 84px at 1920; 'The record' and 'Plate v3' 44px), opsz 36 italic 400 for the verdict pull-quote (28/26/36px), opsz 16 at 400/500/600 and italic 400 for body (19px), options (17px), record statements (19px) and margin (15px). IBM Plex Mono 400/500 for keycaps, kickers, counts, states, Q numbers and paths at 10.5-13px. All embedded as base64 woff2, 179 KB total.
skillOverrides: taste-skill serif discipline: a serif is the default here because the concept is explicitly a publication/interview; Newsreader was chosen (not Fraunces or Instrument Serif) and is paired with a mono, no UI sans.
taste-skill dark-mode-by-default: shipped light-only, using its own exception for print-emulating editorial; the palette is a cool newsprint grey, not the banned warm cream + brass family.
taste-skill rotated-text ban: the two chapter dividers in the filmstrip ('Reopened', 'Deferred') are set vertically because they are real section labels in a 78px strip, not decoration.
taste-skill 'no hand-rolled SVG / real images': the page has no images by design; the only picture is the agent's live prototype in the sandboxed iframe.
ui-ux-pro-max 44px touch targets: desktop-only tool, so the floor is make-interfaces-feel-better's 32-40px for dense desktop; every visible control is at least 32px tall.
Brief key map kept but extended: l flips to the record, / also opens it in find mode, shift+v redraws a stale plate, f is an alias of r.
contractChanges: Child also posts {regions:[{id,x,y,w,h}]} on load and resize (ids and integers only), so the parent can place figure pins over the plate. Demoed by appending a 300-byte listener to VISUAL_HTML before assigning srcdoc; the sandbox (allow-scripts, no same-origin) and postMessage-only contract are unchanged.
